meta.title: Operation of Friability Testing Apparatus in Pharmaceutics Laboratory

sections.purpose: To determine the friability of uncoated tablets by measuring the percentage weight loss due to abrasion during rotation in a drum, as a quality control test as per IP/BP/USP pharmacopeial specifications.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for friability testing of uncoated tablets as a release control and formulation development test — a mandatory IP/BP parameter for tablet quality.
procedure: Weigh 20 tablets (for tablets weighing < 650 mg each) or 10 tablets (for tablets ≥ 650 mg) on an analytical balance accurate to 1 mg; record the initial total weight (W₁).
If applicable, use a de-dusting brush to remove loose dust from the tablet surfaces before weighing.
Place the weighed tablets in the drum of the friability apparatus.
Set the rotation counter to 100 rotations (as per IP/BP/USP).
Switch on the friability tester — the drum should rotate at 25 ± 1 RPM.
Allow the drum to complete 100 rotations (4 minutes at 25 RPM).
After 100 rotations, switch off and remove tablets from the drum.
Remove tablet fragments and dust by de-dusting (brush or blow with compressed air).
Weigh all remaining intact tablets on the same analytical balance; record the final weight (W₂).
Acceptance criterion: Friability should not exceed 1.0% for a single run (IP/BP/USP).
If any tablet shows cracks, chips, or completely breaks, the batch fails regardless of weight loss percentage.
Repeat the test if the friability value is between 0.8–1.0% — use the mean of two runs.
Record tablet identity, weight before and after, number of rotations, and calculated % friability in the batch record.
precautions: Tablets should not be pre-treated (no humidification unless specified) — testing must reflect as-is tablet quality.
Ensure the drum is clean and dry before loading — residual powder from previous test adds to initial weight.
Verify the rotation speed is 25 ± 1 RPM — over-speed gives falsely high friability, under-speed gives falsely low.
For tablets containing large amounts of lubricant (e.g., hard, waxy tablets), pre-wipe the drum to remove static attraction.
Do not mix different product tablets in a single run.
Record all chipped or cracked tablets as failures regardless of weight loss.
Calibrate the tachometer/RPM display of the friability tester regularly.
